blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
British negotiation is usually quiet. There is less pushing and less loud talking. There is no table-thumping. Instead, there is careful conversation. The goal is an agreement that both sides feel good about — and will still respect in six months.

British people use soft words. You will hear "we'd probably need", "it might be difficult", or "I think we could." These words sound gentle. But under the soft words, there are firm positions. Brits just do not say them loudly.

So you must listen carefully. Hedged words often hide the real red lines. "That might be a bit difficult" usually means no. Listen more than you push.

items.q: How is British negotiation usually described?
items.why: "British negotiation is usually quiet… careful conversation."

items.q: What is the goal of the negotiation?
options: An agreement both sides feel good about
To make the other side quiet
items.why: "The goal is an agreement that both sides feel good about."

items.q: What is under the soft British words?
items.why: "under the soft words, there are firm positions."

items.q: "That might be a bit difficult" most likely means…
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que essa frase suave normalmente quer dizer "não".

items.q: The author would most likely AGREE that…
options: You should push hard and talk loudly
Soft words can hide a strong no
items.why: Inferência: o texto todo diz que palavras suaves escondem as verdadeiras linhas vermelhas.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver preparando um colega para uma negociação. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Okay, listen before your meeting. The client is British. He has been very polite, right? Very nice, very calm. But be careful. Polite does not mean yes.

He said the price "might be a bit difficult." That is not a maybe. That is a no. He is telling you no in a soft way. Do not push him. If you push too hard, he will go quiet, not loud.

Listen more than you talk. When he says "we'd probably need more time," he means he definitely needs more time. That is a red line. Do not fight it.

And do not give him an ultimatum. British people do not like ultimatums. They like shared solutions. So ask questions. Give him room. Let him feel comfortable. A calm client says yes more easily than a client under pressure.

One more thing. After he says something soft, there is often silence. That silence is an invitation. He wants you to offer a little more. So be ready.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Oliver say about the client being polite?
options: The client is not really polite
items.why: "Polite does not mean yes."

items.q: What did the client mean by "the price might be a bit difficult"?
items.why: "That is a no. He is telling you no in a soft way."

items.q: What happens if you push a British client too hard?
items.why: "If you push too hard, he will go quiet, not loud."

items.q: Why does Oliver say the silence is an "invitation"?
options: The client did not hear you
The client wants you to offer a little more
The client wants to end the meeting
items.why: Inferência: o silêncio depois de uma frase suave pede que você ofereça um pouco mais.

items.q: What is the best advice Oliver gives?
items.why: Inferência: ele repete ouvir mais, não pressionar e buscar soluções compartilhadas.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We need to negotiate a better price." To negotiate means to…
items.why: To negotiate = negociar, conversar para chegar a um acordo.

items.q: "She likes to hedge her words in a meeting." To hedge means to…
options: speak in a soft, careful way
items.why: To hedge = amenizar, falar de forma suave e cuidadosa.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "For us, that date is a ___ ___ . We cannot change it."
items.why: Red line = linha vermelha, um limite que não pode ser cruzado.

items.q: "His position was clear: no price cut." A position is…
options: the view he holds in a talk
items.why: Position = posição, o ponto de vista que a pessoa defende.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Don't ___ too hard, or the client will stop talking."
items.why: To push = pressionar; pressionar demais faz o cliente ficar quieto.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em negociações. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The boss still has to sign off on the deal." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "The client pushed back on the price." This means the client…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar de algo.

items.q: "Let's hold off for a week before we decide." To hold off means to…
items.why: Hold off = esperar, adiar por um tempo.

items.q: "They agreed, but they never followed through." This means they…
options: did not finish what they promised
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "A soft no won't move the needle for us." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = fazer diferença perceptível; aqui, não muda nada.
